dossier.purpose: Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (CLI `srt`, npm package @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime): a Node/TypeScript CLI and library that wraps an arbitrary command in OS-level filesystem and network restrictions without a container. On Linux it generates a bubblewrap (bwrap) invocation (read-only root bind with selective writable binds, deny masks, network/PID/user namespaces, --cap-drop ALL) plus a bundled seccomp helper that blocks AF_UNIX socket creation. On macOS it generates a Seatbelt (SBPL) profile run through /usr/bin/sandbox-exec. Windows (alpha) uses a dedicated local user, WFP filters and ACLs. Network access is deny-by-default and mediated by host-side HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 proxies that enforce a domain allow/deny list (no network namespace interfaces on Linux; localhost-proxy-only Seatbelt rules on macOS). Reads are allow-by-default, writes deny-by-default. WSL2 is not mentioned in the README; the code treats WSL2 as ordinary Linux and rejects only WSL1. Built for Claude Code and published as a 0.0.x 'Beta Research Preview'. Method note: this dossier is a static reading of README, source, tests and CI at v0.0.78; nothing was built or executed (no shell was available in this session).

claims.claim: Lightweight tool for enforcing filesystem and network restrictions on arbitrary processes at the OS level, without requiring a container; uses sandbox-exec on macOS and bubblewrap on Linux plus proxy-based network filtering; usable for agents, local MCP servers and bash commands.
Beta Research Preview developed for Claude Code; APIs and configuration formats may evolve.
Secure-by-default: processes start with minimal access and the user pokes only the holes needed.

Filesystem: reads allowed everywhere by default (deny-then-allow; allowRead beats denyRead); writes denied everywhere by default (allow-only; denyWrite beats allowWrite); empty allowWrite means no write access.

Network is allow-only: all network access denied by default, empty allowedDomains means no network; HTTP/HTTPS go through a host HTTP proxy and other TCP through a SOCKS5 proxy, both enforcing domain allow/deny lists (deniedDomains checked first).
Linux: the sandboxed process's network namespace is removed entirely; all traffic must pass through host proxies reached over Unix sockets bind-mounted into the sandbox (socat bridging).
macOS: the Seatbelt profile allows communication only to the specific localhost port(s) where the proxies listen.

With no ~/.srt-settings.json, srt uses built-in defaults (no network, no writes outside the default write paths, unrestricted reads); a settings file that exists but is empty, unreadable or invalid (or a missing --settings file) is an error and srt exits instead of falling back.
Unix sockets are blocked by default on both platforms; on Linux via seccomp (x64/arm64 only); if seccomp is not available, sockets are unrestricted and a warning is shown.

Linux requires bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep; Ubuntu 24.04+ needs kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 (or an AppArmor profile granting userns); a root caller needs CAP_SETFCAP in its bounding set.

Some files/directories are always write-blocked even inside allowed write paths (.bashrc, .zshrc, .gitconfig, .mcp.json, .vscode/, .idea/, .claude/commands/, .claude/agents/, .git/hooks/, .git/config); on Linux nested ones are found by a ripgrep scan to depth 3 by default.
Violation detection: macOS taps the system sandbox log store; on Linux bubblewrap has no built-in violation reporting (use strace).

Known limits: domain allowlists can still permit exfiltration (e.g. github.com) and may be bypassed by domain fronting; allowUnixSockets can expose powerful services; enableWeakerNestedSandbox considerably weakens Linux security; Linux proxy use relies on environment variables that some programs ignore.
Windows support is alpha (dedicated srt-sandbox local user, WFP egress fence, per-session ACLs; one-time elevated windows-install).

install.method: Linux system dependencies, Debian/Ubuntu (README lists each tool separately; dnf and pacman equivalents are given)
install.command: apt-get install bubblewrap; apt-get install socat; apt-get install ripgrep

install.method: Ubuntu 24.04+ prerequisite: allow capability-bearing unprivileged user namespaces
macOS dependency listed by README (code does not use ripgrep on macOS, see claim_checks)
From source (development); Linux seccomp helper must be built separately (needs bun, gcc, libseccomp-dev)
install.command: npm install && npm run build  (then, on Linux: npm run build:seccomp)

install.method: Optional toolchain the README documents as a seccomp fallback for other architectures (no runtime compile exists in code, see claim_checks)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - README Linux section (README.md:547-572); CI job on ubuntu-latest x86-64, including a second run against source-built bubblewrap 0.12.0 (.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml:18-20, 205-225); release builds the x64 apply-seccomp helper (.github/workflows/release.yml:21-25).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - README.md never mentions WSL. Code treats WSL2+ as ordinary Linux (src/utils/platform.ts:43-50) and rejects only WSL1 (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:1014-1019; WSL version read from /proc/version, src/utils/platform.ts:13-37). No WSL2 CI leg (integration-tests.yml:14-37) and no WSL2-specific test (test/utils/platform.test.ts:5-13). Works only if the WSL2 kernel permits bwrap user/PID/net namespaces (README.md:562-568), which the repo does not show.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - README macOS via sandbox-exec, no extra dependencies (README.md:107, 541); CI on macos-14 arm64 and macos-15-large x86-64 (integration-tests.yml:24-29); code runs /usr/bin/sandbox-exec (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:1473-1484).
platforms.gpu: unknown - no GPU/CUDA/Metal handling in README or src. On Linux /dev is replaced by bwrap's minimal devtmpfs (src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:905-906; src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:3215-3216) and /dev/* entries in write lists are skipped (linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1978-1982), so no documented option exposes GPU device nodes; the macOS profile allows only two IOKit user-client classes (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:1039-1044).

integrations.cli: yes - `srt` binary (package.json:8-10; src/cli.ts:177-300): `srt [command...]`, `-c <command>`, `-d/--debug`, `-s/--settings <path>` (default ~/.srt-settings.json, src/cli.ts:19-21), `--control-fd <fd>` for live network-allowlist updates (README.md:187-221), `--version`; plus windows-install / windows-uninstall subcommands (src/cli.ts:190-269).
integrations.mcp: none found as an MCP server or client (no MCP code in src/). README documents wrapping third-party MCP servers by using `srt` as the command in .mcp.json (README.md:50-101).
integrations.sdk_or_api: TypeScript/Node library: `import { SandboxManager } from '@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime'` (src/index.ts:2; package.json:6-7; README.md:223-303) exposing initialize(), wrapWithSandbox(), wrapWithSandboxArgv(), updateConfig(), reset(), cleanupAfterCommand(), annotateStderrWithSandboxFailures(), violation store (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:2418-2517). No HTTP API or daemon.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: README says it was developed for Claude Code and links its sandboxing docs (README.md:9, 132-135); code carries Claude-specific names: /tmp/claude and ~/.claude/debug default write paths (src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:527-546), .claude/commands and .claude/agents mandatory denies (sandbox-utils.ts:34-40), CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR (sandbox-utils.ts:704-708), claude-http-*.sock bridge sockets (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1189), CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_*_PROXY_PORT env vars (linux-sandbox-utils.ts:3182-3195). Codex: none found (no codex/openai mention anywhere in the repo).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or call-home code found: src/ makes no fetch/http(s).request calls and contains no external URLs (only 127.0.0.1/localhost/placeholder strings); no accounts, API keys or cloud services are required; README says nothing about telemetry. Network behaviour: (1) the library starts a loopback-only mux proxy (HTTP/CONNECT + SOCKS5) on 127.0.0.1, port 0 on macOS/Linux, protected by a per-session random auth token (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:603-626, 926-941; src/sandbox/http-proxy.ts:250-264; src/sandbox/socks-proxy.ts:88-101); it dials upstream only for destinations the policy allows, after a resolved-address check (src/sandbox/resolved-address-guard.ts:1-24). (2) HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY in srt's own environment are adopted as a parent proxy (src/sandbox/parent-proxy.ts:70-85), and the resolved-address check is skipped for that hop (README.md:365). (3) Local helper processes only: socat bridges on Linux (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1195-1204), `npm root -g` to locate a global install (src/sandbox/generate-seccomp-filter.ts:15-41), `log stream` on macOS (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:1526). Install time: npm registry only (.npmrc:1); no consumer install hooks (package.json:14-27 has only `prepare: husky`, a dev hook). Windows only: windows-install creates a local user, registry state and WFP filters (README.md:602-610). The child gets SANDBOX_RUNTIME=1 (src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:696).

entry_points.what: CLI built to dist/cli.js and exposed as bin `srt`: default command runs the wrapped command; options -c, -d/--debug, -s/--settings, --control-fd, --version; subcommands windows-install / windows-uninstall (src/cli.ts:177-300; package.json:8-10).

Library entry (package main dist/index.js): exports SandboxManager, SandboxViolationStore, zod config schemas and types, LinuxSandboxProfileError, Windows install/status helpers, getWslVersion (src/index.ts:1-130; package.json:6-7).
SandboxManager singleton: initialize() (line 633), wrapWithSandbox() (1635), wrapWithSandboxArgv() (1878), updateConfig() (2034), plus the exported API object (2484-2517).

Static C helper run inside bwrap on Linux: nested user+PID+mount namespaces, PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 init, seccomp filter blocking socket(AF_UNIX) and io_uring, optional USER_NOTIF write observer; built by vendor/seccomp/build.ts into vendor/seccomp/<arch>/apply-seccomp.
Rust Windows helper srt-win (user provisioning, WFP filters, ACLs, two-hop launch); built by vendor/srt-win/build.ts; Windows only, alpha.
JVM -javaagent injected through JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS so Java tools honour the proxy; built to vendor/java-proxy-agent/srt-proxy-agent.jar (vendor/java-proxy-agent/build.ts).

code.architecture: TypeScript ESM package (Node >=20.11.0) with one CLI and one library sharing a module-level SandboxManager singleton (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:132-137, 2484-2517; about 2.5k lines). Config: zod v3 schemas (src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts; `network` and `filesystem` blocks required, :1109-1112) loaded by the CLI from ~/.srt-settings.json via src/utils/config-loader.ts. initialize() checks dependencies, then starts a loopback mux proxy (mux-proxy.ts) fronting an HTTP/CONNECT proxy (http-proxy.ts) and a SOCKS5 proxy (socks-proxy.ts, library @pondwader/socks5-server); both call filterNetworkRequest (deny list, then allow list, else deny; sandbox-manager.ts:332-410) with a per-session auth token and a resolved-address guard (resolved-address-guard.ts). Optional extras: parent proxy (parent-proxy.ts), experimental TLS termination with per-host leaf certs (tls-terminate-proxy.ts, mitm-ca.ts, mitm-leaf.ts via node-forge, request-filter.ts), credential masking/injection (credential-*.ts, aws-sigv4.ts, body-substitution.ts), JVM proxy agent (java-proxy-agent.ts). wrapWithSandbox() returns a shell string for the caller to spawn. Linux backend (linux-sandbox-utils.ts, about 3.3k lines): bwrap argv with --ro-bind / / plus writable binds for allowWrite (:1950-1956), tmpfs or /dev/null masks for denyRead/denyWrite and mandatory paths (ripgrep scan, src/utils/ripgrep.ts), --unshare-net (:3115-3118), --unshare-pid, --unshare-user, --cap-drop ALL, fresh --proc, --new-session --die-with-parent (:3033, 3225-3255); host socat bridges Unix sockets to the proxy and in-sandbox socat listens on 3128/1080 (:1195-1204, 1377-1379); apply-seccomp adds a nested namespace and the AF_UNIX/io_uring seccomp filter; optional write-violation observer (linux-violation-monitor.ts). macOS backend (macos-sandbox-utils.ts, about 1.6k lines): SBPL profile starting `(deny default)` run via /usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p (:968-970, 1473-1484); violations read from `log stream` (:1526). Windows backend (windows-sandbox-utils.ts + Rust vendor/srt-win-src) is alpha. Denies and violations are collected in sandbox-violation-store.ts.
code.packaging_and_release: Published to npm as @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime, version 0.0.78 equal to the tag (package.json:2-3). `files` ships dist/, vendor/seccomp, vendor/srt-win, vendor/java-proxy-agent, README.md, LICENSE (package.json:53-60). The helper binaries (apply-seccomp x64/arm64, srt-win.exe x64/arm64, srt-proxy-agent.jar) are gitignored build outputs (.gitignore:5-10), built in the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml:16-90), packed and content-checked (92-175), smoke-installed on Windows (177-218) and published from the packed tarball (220-243). Triggers: GitHub release published, plus pull_request which runs everything except publish (release.yml:3-8). Guards: release tag must be an ancestor of origin/main and match the package.json version (101-118). Publishing uses npm trusted publishing via OIDC (id-token: write, environment npm, 226-243); a workflow comment says provenance is attached automatically (242) - not verifiable from the repo. No checksum files, detached signatures or GitHub release assets are produced; all actions are pinned by commit SHA. No other distribution channel (image, brew, standalone binary) found in the repo.
code.tests_and_ci: bun test (package.json:17) with bun:test and fast-check property tests: 83 *.test.ts files (7 in test/, 72 in test/sandbox/, 4 in test/utils/), plus test/utils/which-node-test.mjs, 7 helper modules in test/helpers/ and AWS SigV4 vectors in test/fixtures/. Tests are platform-gated (describe.if(isLinux) at test/sandbox/integration.test.ts:58; describe.if(isMacOS) at test/sandbox/macos-seatbelt.test.ts:34) and run real sandboxed commands (empty-allowlist network block, writes outside cwd blocked, PID namespace, symlink escape, mandatory deny, seccomp). Two workflows only. .github/workflows/integration-tests.yml (push to main and every PR): matrix Linux x86-64 (ubuntu-latest) and arm64 (ubuntu-24.04-arm), macOS x86-64 (macos-15-large) and arm64 (macos-14), Windows x86-64 and arm64 (lines 14-37); Linux installs bubblewrap, libseccomp-dev, gcc, socat, ripgrep, apparmor-profiles, zsh, disables the AppArmor userns restriction and checks bwrap can nest namespaces (147-168); runs eslint (linux x86-64 only), tsc typecheck, builds the seccomp helper and JVM agent, `npm test`, then re-runs `npm test` against a source-built bubblewrap 0.12.0 (205-225) and a Node fallback test (227-229); Windows legs run cargo build/test/clippy, the smoke scripts and a subset of the TS tests (66-145); a docker-tests job runs test/docker-weak-sandbox.test.ts in ubuntu:24.04 as uid 0 with and without CAP_SYS_ADMIN (241-295). release.yml also runs on pull requests (build + pack, no publish). No WSL2 leg, no coverage step, no CodeQL or dependabot config. Local: husky pre-commit runs lint-staged (eslint, prettier) (.husky/pre-commit; package.json:82-87).
code.dependencies: package.json: 4 runtime dependencies (@pondwader/socks5-server ^1.0.10, commander ^12.1.0, node-forge ^1.4.0 [lockfile license (BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0)], zod ^3.25.0; imported as zod/v3, src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:14) and 17 devDependencies (package.json:28-52); package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) shows no nested dependencies for the four runtime packages. vendor/srt-win-src/Cargo.toml: 6 direct crates, all under cfg(windows) (anyhow, clap, serde, serde_json, windows, rusqlite[bundled]); Cargo.lock present; rust-toolchain.toml pins Rust 1.98.1. code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md or disclosure/contact policy anywhere in the tree (globs for SECURITY*, *security*.md, CONTRIBUTING*, CHANGELOG* all empty); .github/ holds only the two workflow files. README has a 'Security Limitations' section (README.md:881-893) but no reporting process.

claim_checks.claim: Linux: network namespace removed, all traffic via host proxies over bind-mounted Unix sockets; empty allowedDomains means no network (README.md:122-124, 355).
claim_checks.evidence: --unshare-net is added whenever network restriction is on (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:3115-3118); proxy sockets are bound in (3123-3145) and bridged by socat (host 1195-1204, inside 1377-1379). filterNetworkRequest checks deniedDomains, then allowedDomains, else denies (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:366-393); the CLI passes no ask callback (src/cli.ts:431). Tests assert HTTP, HTTPS, DNS and wget are blocked with empty allowedDomains (test/sandbox/integration.test.ts:993-1147). Caveat: restriction is decided by allowedDomains !== undefined (sandbox-manager.ts:1741-1757); the zod schema requires the key (src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:720-726) but initialize() does not run the schema (only src/utils/config-loader.ts does), so a non-TypeScript library caller that omits it gets no network restriction. Static reading; not executed.

claim_checks.claim: macOS: Seatbelt profile run through sandbox-exec; network allowed only to the localhost proxy port(s) (README.md:107, 126).
claim_checks.evidence: Profile starts `(deny default ...)` (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:968-970); `(allow network*)` is emitted only when no network restriction is configured (1144-1145), otherwise only localhost proxy ports plus optional allowLocalBinding / Unix-socket allowances (1147-1230); command is `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p <profile> <shell> -c <cmd>` (1473-1484). CI runs macOS arm64 and x86-64 (.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml:24-29). Not executed here.

claim_checks.claim: Filesystem model: reads allowed by default, writes denied by default (README.md:117-120).
claim_checks.evidence: Linux binds / read-only then adds writable binds only for allowWrite paths (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1950-1956); macOS emits `(allow file-read*)` then denies (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:784-800) and restricts writes in generateWriteRules (869-885). Source comments call reads 'maximally permissive by default' and writes 'maximally restrictive' (src/sandbox/sandbox-schemas.ts:18, 42). Built-in CLI defaults have empty denyRead and allowWrite (src/cli.ts:65-78). `filesystem.disabled: true` drops all filesystem rules (network rules still apply) and is not in the README option list (src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:897-907).

claim_checks.claim: Settings handling: missing default file gives built-in defaults; empty, unreadable or invalid file, or a missing --settings file, makes srt refuse to run (README.md:177-185).
claim_checks.evidence: src/cli.ts:309-343 and refuseSettings at 48-54; loader classes in src/utils/config-loader.ts:46-90; covered by test/cli.test.ts:163-277.

claim_checks.claim: Basic Usage transcript (README.md:19-37): `srt "curl anthropic.com"` succeeds with 'Running: ...' output and `srt "cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa"` is blocked.
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from README. Positional args are shell-quoted one by one (src/cli.ts:483-489; src/utils/shell-quote.ts:26-46) and a test pins that an argument containing spaces stays one token (test/cli.test.ts:130-138), so one quoted string runs as a single command name; 'Running:' is printed nowhere in src/ (only README.md:22-35); and the built-in defaults have empty allowedDomains and denyRead (src/cli.ts:65-78), so anthropic.com and ~/.ssh behave as shown only with a settings file that allows/denies them. Working forms are `srt curl anthropic.com` or `srt -c 'curl anthropic.com'`.

claim_checks.claim: Certain files/directories are always write-blocked even inside allowed write paths (README.md:756-772).
claim_checks.evidence: The lists match code (src/sandbox/sandbox-utils.ts:11-40; src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:282-318; src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:96-129) but are anchored at process.cwd() (test/sandbox/mandatory-deny-paths.test.ts:44-45), so write roots outside cwd get no such denies. On Linux nested matches come from a ripgrep scan of cwd limited to depth 3 by default (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:1543; linux-sandbox-utils.ts:360-373) that skips node_modules (367-368). `filesystem.disabled` turns them off (sandbox-config.ts:901-906).

claim_checks.claim: Unix sockets blocked by default; on Linux via seccomp for x64/arm64, with a warning if seccomp is unavailable; gcc/libseccomp-dev needed as fallback on other architectures (README.md:396-399, 574-582, 808-832).
claim_checks.evidence: Filter blocks socket(AF_UNIX) and io_uring (vendor/seccomp-src/seccomp-unix-block.c:92-121); helper makes nested namespaces and aborts rather than falling back (vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c:1-30, 711-757). Only x64/arm64 prebuilt binaries are looked up (src/sandbox/generate-seccomp-filter.ts:133-157); nothing compiles a filter at runtime, so the README's gcc/libseccomp 'fallback' does not exist in code (compilers are used only by `npm run build:seccomp`, vendor/seccomp/build.ts). Without the helper the wrap still proceeds with Unix sockets unrestricted (linux-sandbox-utils.ts:3046-3051); the 'warning' is a checkDependencies() warning that initialize() ignores (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:683-688; linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1075-1080) plus a debug log printed only when SRT_DEBUG is set (src/utils/debug.ts:11-13), so the srt CLI is silent unless run with --debug. The helper binaries are gitignored (.gitignore:5-6) and exist only in the npm package.

claim_checks.claim: README Platform Support lists macOS, Linux and Windows (alpha) (README.md:539-543); WSL2 is not mentioned.
claim_checks.evidence: README.md contains no WSL text. Code returns 'linux' for WSL2+ with the comment 'same sandboxing' (src/utils/platform.ts:47-50) and isSupportedPlatform() rejects only WSL1 (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:1014-1019). No WSL2 CI leg (.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml:14-37) and no WSL2 test (test/utils/platform.test.ts:5-13). Support is by code intent only; no run on WSL2 is evidenced in the repo.

ripgrep is invoked only from Linux code (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:10, 360 via src/utils/ripgrep.ts); the dependency check is Linux-only (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:1047-1054) and a macOS comment says no ripgrep is needed there (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:887-888). CI still installs it on macOS (integration-tests.yml:170-173). The README's architecture tree is also stale: it lists src/utils/settings.ts and exec.ts (README.md:143-147) which do not exist; src/utils holds config-loader, debug, platform, ripgrep, shell-quote, which.

claim_checks.claim: Linux: bubblewrap provides no violation reporting; use strace (README.md:849-860).
claim_checks.evidence: bwrap itself reports nothing, but the library ships an opt-in Linux monitor: apply-seccomp reports write-intent syscalls over a Unix socket and the manager filters them against allow/deny paths (src/sandbox/linux-violation-monitor.ts:61-81; src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:699-744; vendor/seccomp-src/apply-seccomp.c:96, 254). It is on only when a library caller passes enableLogMonitor (sandbox-manager.ts:633-637); the srt CLI does not (src/cli.ts:431). Its own comment calls the events diagnostic hints because the reported path is attacker-controlled and racy (linux-violation-monitor.ts:72-75). Proxy denies are recorded on all platforms (sandbox-manager.ts:338-341); macOS reads the system log (macos-sandbox-utils.ts:1509-1532).

risks: WSL2 and Linux prerequisites: WSL2 is neither documented, tested nor special-cased. README.md never mentions WSL; CI has no WSL2 leg (.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml:14-37); code treats WSL2+ as plain Linux and rejects only WSL1 (src/utils/platform.ts:43-50; src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:1014-1019). Linux enforcement needs bwrap, socat and ripgrep on PATH and capability-bearing unprivileged user namespaces (README.md:547-568). initialize() checks the binaries but, for a non-root caller, does not probe whether namespaces can be created (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1050-1117), and CI must switch off Ubuntu's AppArmor userns restriction to pass (integration-tests.yml:153-168).

Secret exposure by default: reads are allow-by-default and the CLI's built-in config has empty denyRead (src/cli.ts:65-78; README.md:117-119, 177-180; src/sandbox/sandbox-schemas.ts:18), so files such as ~/.ssh stay readable unless the settings file denies them. The child inherits the caller's environment except variables named in the `credentials` config (no env clearing in src/; src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:3086-3095; src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:1460-1469). That credentials block (mask/deny files and env vars with proxy-side substitution, src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:319-700) is barely documented (README.md:457 only) and file masking degrades to deny on macOS (sandbox-config.ts:315-317).

Network policy limits: filtering is by host name, so allowed domains can still carry exfiltration and domain fronting may bypass it (README.md:879-887). The resolved-address guard denies loopback, link-local, metadata and this host's own addresses by default but private ranges only if listed in deniedResolvedAddresses, and it is skipped for parentProxy/mitmProxy hops, including a proxy picked up from HTTP_PROXY (README.md:361-367, 883; src/sandbox/resolved-address-guard.ts:59-76; src/sandbox/parent-proxy.ts:70-85). TLS termination and credential injection are marked experimental (src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:880-883). On macOS allowLocalBinding lets the child reach loopback ports without the proxy (README.md:365).

Linux Unix-socket blocking depends on a prebuilt helper that exists only in the npm tarball and only for x64/arm64 (src/sandbox/generate-seccomp-filter.ts:133-157; .gitignore:5-6; .github/workflows/release.yml:132). When absent the sandbox still runs with Unix sockets unrestricted and the CLI prints no warning unless --debug is set (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:1075-1080, 3046-3051; src/utils/debug.ts:11-13; src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:683-688). allowUnixSockets is ignored on Linux (README.md:391-393). enableWeakerNestedSandbox binds the host /proc instead of a fresh one (linux-sandbox-utils.ts:3246-3255; README.md:891).

Boundary scope and opt-outs: mandatory write-deny paths are anchored at the process cwd, the Linux nested scan is depth 3 by default and skips node_modules (src/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.ts:282-318, 360-373; src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:96-129; test/sandbox/mandatory-deny-paths.test.ts:44-45). Plain config flags weaken or disable the boundary: filesystem.disabled (src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:897-907), enableWeakerNestedSandbox, allowAllUnixSockets, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation (trustd exfil vector) and allowAppleEvents (child can launch unsandboxed apps) (README.md:462-465, 891-893). On Linux a file outside the write paths that already has a hard link inside one can be written through it (README.md:736).

macOS reliance on sandbox-exec: enforcement is a generated SBPL profile passed to /usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p (src/sandbox/macos-sandbox-utils.ts:968-970, 1473-1484); the code works around sandbox-exec limits (string literals over 1025 bytes invalidate a profile, thousands of path filters compile slowly: macos-sandbox-utils.ts:550-555, 580-589; test/sandbox/macos-profile-size.test.ts), and the README's only SBPL reference is a 2011 third-party PDF (README.md:107). Go programs need enableWeakerNetworkIsolation to verify TLS under a MITM proxy (README.md:464). The repo makes no statement about Apple's support policy for this interface.

Embedding model: SandboxManager is a module-level singleton, one config and one proxy allowlist per process (src/sandbox/sandbox-manager.ts:132-137, 2484-2517). Per-call customConfig can change filesystem rules but the domain lists are read from the shared global config by the proxy (sandbox-manager.ts:332-410, 1674-1697, 1741-1757), so concurrent tasks cannot hold different domain allowlists in one process. initialize() does not validate the config object (only src/utils/config-loader.ts runs the schema). updateConfig() and --control-fd change only network lists for a running command; filesystem rules are baked in at wrap time (sandbox-manager.ts:2015-2030; README.md:187-196).

Maturity, process and build: version 0.0.78 labelled 'Beta Research Preview ... APIs and configuration formats may evolve' (package.json:3; README.md:7-9). No SECURITY.md/disclosure policy, CONTRIBUTING or CHANGELOG in the tree. Tests record earlier enforcement bugs that were fixed: empty allowedDomains once meant unrestricted network (test/sandbox/wrap-with-sandbox.test.ts:547-557) and a macOS rename-based read bypass (test/sandbox/macos-seatbelt.test.ts:20-32). README lags the code: Basic Usage transcript (README.md:19-37), architecture tree (143-147), macOS ripgrep requirement (584-588), seccomp gcc fallback (574-582), and 'custom proxy not yet supported' (877) versus network.httpProxyPort/socksProxyPort/mitmProxy/parentProxy in src/sandbox/sandbox-config.ts:790-810, 885-890. A git checkout lacks the enforcement helpers (apply-seccomp, srt-win.exe, JVM jar are gitignored, .gitignore:5-10) and needs Bun plus gcc/libseccomp-dev, Rust 1.98.1 or a JDK to build them (package.json:15-18; rust-toolchain.toml:5); tests run under Bun 1.4.2 while the CLI runs on Node >=20.11 (integration-tests.yml:51-54; package.json:11-13). The only release artifact is the npm tarball; provenance relies on npm trusted publishing, asserted in a workflow comment (release.yml:242-243) and not checkable from the repo.
